read: A quieter pre-holiday session, led by two stories: Bayer paid $150m upfront for a Phase 1 Hansoh ADC in a deal worth up to $3.25bn, and BMS's Sotyktu split its two pivotal lupus trials. China-sourced ADCs remain the default way for big pharma to restock oncology, despite the House China committee report earlier this week. In I&I, the bar for oral drugs keeps rising. The day after Kymera's Dupixent-like STAT6 data, a TYK2 inhibitor that wins one SLE trial and loses the other on placebo response will struggle to command a premium. On pricing, Bayer pulling Kerendia from Germany and the Amgen-BMS Opdivo settlement (US biosimilar entry fixed for October 2028) show LOE and European reimbursement now drive strategy as much as pipelines do. Tone: biotech held Monday-Tuesday's sharp rebound (XBI -0.14% on Wednesday) through a hot PCE print and a new US tariff proposal that exempts pharma. Risk appetite is intact but the market is selective.

items.headline: Bayer in-licenses Hansoh's EGFR/c-Met bispecific ADC HS-20122 for up to $3.25bn
items.detail: $150m upfront plus up to $3.1bn in development, regulatory and sales milestones and tiered royalties, for rights outside Greater China. The asset is Phase 1 (solid tumours, NSCLC lead), and the licence starts once antitrust clearance is received. Bayer is buying an ADC version of the EGFR/MET biology that J&J's Rybrevant validated, entering a space where AbbVie's c-Met ADC Emrelis is already on the market. Hansoh (HKEX: 3692) is now the go-to Chinese ADC shop for big pharma.

items.headline: Bristol Myers Squibb: Sotyktu (deucravacitinib) hits in POETYK SLE-1 and misses in POETYK SLE-2
items.detail: Two 52-week Phase 3 trials (n=510 and n=513; 3 mg BID on top of standard of care). SLE-1 met SRI-4 and was also significant on BICLA, SRI-4 with steroid taper and fatigue. SLE-2 showed a similar drug response but missed because the placebo response was higher, with numerical gains on every key secondary. BMS will review the data with regulators. One hit and one miss makes a clean filing harder and dents a key LOE-offset indication for a TYK2 inhibitor already marketed in psoriasis. A Sjogren's Phase 3 reads out in 2027. Roche's Gazyva SLE decision is due in December.

items.headline: Amgen settles with BMS and Ono: US Opdivo biosimilar ABP 206 can launch 1 October 2028
items.detail: Terms are confidential. FDA action on the biosimilar is expected by year-end. The settlement fixes the LOE date for a drug with more than $5.9bn in US sales last year, consistent with BMS's 2028 exclusivity guidance. It removes litigation risk for both sides and gives Amgen's biosimilars unit a defined 2028 driver.

items.headline: Bayer will withdraw Kerendia (finerenone) from Germany on 15 December, in all indications
items.detail: The trigger was the G-BA's October finding of no added benefit in HFmrEF/HFpEF (LVEF of 40% or more), which left the reimbursed price commercially unviable. Kerendia's 9M sales rose 73% to EUR977m, mainly from the US and China. Barclays puts German revenue below EUR50m, so the financial hit is small. The move signals that European pharma is pushing back on AMNOG-style pricing as US MFN links US and EU prices.

items.headline: GSK: twice-yearly Exdensur (depemokimab) is non-inferior to monthly Nucala in EGPA (Phase 3 OCEAN)
items.detail: Dosing twice a year matched Nucala's efficacy, which gives GSK a convenience-led switch argument inside its own IL-5 franchise and against AstraZeneca's Fasenra (monthly). It is a lifecycle defence as Nucala ages.

items.headline: Arife, the BioNTech founders' new mRNA oncology company, is reportedly raising about $1bn, led by Plural
items.detail: The FT reports that Sahin and Tureci are in talks ahead of stepping down from BioNTech. BioNTech has said it will contribute mRNA technology and rights for a minority stake plus milestones and royalties. This would be among the largest European biotech launches ever, and the terms of the BNTX carve-out deserve close scrutiny.

items.headline: Policy: US proposes Section 301 "overcapacity" tariffs on 14 economies; pharma is exempt
items.detail: The proposed rates are up to 20% (15% for the EU, Japan, Korea and Switzerland, in line with their deals), plus 20% stacked on existing duties for China (40% if the truce collapses). They are expected in January at the earliest, after hearings. Goods already under sectoral duties, including pharmaceuticals, are excluded, so the direct impact on the sector is limited. The risk is to the US-China truce, which expires in January.

items.headline: Market: biotech holds its rebound through a hot PCE print
items.detail: XBI slipped 0.14% to 156.60 on Wednesday after a roughly 6% surge on Tuesday. It is up about 12% from the 20 November close of 140.18, despite October core PCE at 3.3% (versus 3.2% expected) and a sharp intraday fall in the Nasdaq. Wednesday's NBI figure could not be verified.

items.headline: GLP-1 NAION warning (update): Lilly has already added the language to its labels; Health Canada issues its own warning
items.detail: Bloomberg reports that final FDA class wording may land early next year, with hundreds of NAION suits pending against Novo and Lilly. Novo disputes causation. The litigation is now the overhang rather than prescribing.

items.headline: Novo Nordisk: outgoing CFO Karsten Munk Knudsen will run the Lundbeck Foundation from 1 January; Luigi La Corte succeeds him as Novo CFO
items.detail: The departure itself was known. The successor name, per Bloomberg, completes the finance handover.

items.headline: Capricor flags layoffs after the second deramiocel rejection
items.detail: Headcount has not been disclosed. The company is preparing to fight the FDA, which cited data-integrity issues.

items.headline: Neuralink gets FDA approval to start LINK, the first US pivotal trial of an implantable BCI (ALS paralysis)
items.detail: This is a device IDE, not a marketing approval. It is a read-across for the BCI and neurotech private market.
